title: Gheorghe Hagi appointed Romania head coach: ‘I was born to win, not just to exist’
content:
Romania have appointed Gheorghe Hagi, widely considered the nation’s greatest ever soccer player, as their new men’s national team coach.

The 61-year-old replaces Mircea Lucescu, who passed away earlier this month aged 80, less than two weeks after overseeing Romania’s World Cup playoff defeat to Turkey.

Hagi has been appointed on a four-year contract, meaning the former playmaker will take charge of the qualification campaigns for the European Championship in 2028 and the 2030 World Cup.

“Our goal is to win every game. Our goal is to win the Nations League. Our goal is to qualify for the European Championship,” Hagi told at a press conference in Bucharest on Monday, in quotes carried by Romania’s press agency Agerpres.

“I was born to win, not just to exist.

“It is an honour and a great responsibility to represent Romania once again.”

Lucescu, Hagi’s predeccessor, was Romania coach when Hagi made his international debut aged 18 before being made captain two years later.

“He wanted me to take over as coach,” Hagi said of Lucescu at Romania, who have not qualified for a World Cup since 1998. Hagi’s son Ianis is the vice-captain of the national team.

Hagi — who scored over 300 goals across his senior playing career — played for Romania in three World Cups, in 1990, 1994 (where he was named in the World Cup All-Star Team after helping his nation to the quarter-final stage in the U.S.) and 1998; as well as in three European Championships, in 1984, 1996 and 2000.

At club level, Hagi spent two seasons each at Real Madrid and Barcelona, before moving to Galatasaray, where he won four successive league titles, the UEFA Cup and Super Cup.

Hagi was nominated six times for the Ballon d’Or and ranked fourth in the rankings in 1994.

After retiring from playing, Hagi coached Romania for four matches in 2001. “I was young and restless then,” Hagi said on Monday of that stint. “I’m different now. More experienced, more of a coach in every way.”

He had two stints in charge of Galatasaray and, in 2009, he founded Viitorul Constanta — with an emphasis on developing young players —  and became the club’s manager in 2014, winning the Romanian league title three years later.

In 2021, Viitorul merged with Farul Constanta and two years later, Hagi coached the club to the Romanian title.
